body: Actually, scratch that, my eyesight failing me, this needs a double check the second init is redundant.

I came across this once and while this is an obvious performance hole, I think it's one not fixed so easily.

The key insight is that `memnew_placement(&VariantInternalAccessor<T>::get(v), T);` isn't actually guaranteed to initialize the pointee. It is skipped for primitives such as `double`.

Here you can see it demonstrated clearly: https://godbolt.org/z/1W3aTr7ah

In practice, it still happens to be correct most times because `clear()` happens to reset the payload to `0` for most types, and most types happen to default to `0`. However, I wouldn't put my hand in the fire for this. Even if happens to be true for all types today (I haven't checked), it would be relying on UB.

I think to properly fix the double initialization, more parts of the initialization logic have to be refactored. High time, but will require a good amount of sleuthing work.

Thinking about this again, I think the new version is the right trade-off for the moment.

What we lose: primitive types are sometimes initialized twice (but probably 'optimized away').
What we gain: Allocation types are not initialized twice needlessly.

So it should be overall a safe and needed performance improvement. But nuances are hard so this should be merged early in the cycle.

The unit tests are a little verbose for my taste, but they're acceptable. I wouldn't say a 'templated' version would be strictly better so we can leave them as is.

As a note to the future: This essentially increases the guarantee of `VariantInitializer` to produce the type's default value.
